correctness.rationale: The proof works for every finite k and extended diameters: in a zero-hyperbolic first factor two opposite-pair sums equal A. If A>D each max-metric pairing sum is <=A+D, with two >=A. If A<=D all six distances <=D, and the sum of the two smaller pair sums dominates the largest, giving largest gap <=D. The geodesic square in the two largest trees gives exact lower bound D/2 via compass quartet. D=0 and D=infinity handled separately. The included actual verify.py passed 14,680,587 exact rational finite quartets across 9 finite cases. No finite test is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Products of tree metrics are fundamental models for hyperbolicity. The new formula gives a complete and sharp diameter-vector invariant for all finite maximum-metric products of real trees including unbounded factors; unlike the newly established sum-product partition theorem, only the second largest diameter matters. It classifies exactly when finite sup products are Gromov hyperbolic and establishes a general sharp-order perturbation upper bound for one zero-hyperbolic factor times arbitrary bounded metric geometry. This is a motivated structural theorem, not a routine normalization or arbitrary low-dimensional example.
